newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund vol set to slide to 5.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund vol set to slide to 5.5 pct.

text.p: Bund volatility of options traded on LIFFE was eyeing the downside on Tuesday, but was unlikely to break through the 5.5 percent support ahead of key U.S. data at the end of the week, traders said.
There was little fundamental news driving the market, with most traders' attention firmly fixed on Friday's U.S. producer prices and retail sales data.

"Very short term volatility will head down to reflect how quiet things are," said a trader at a U.S. bank in London. "But it will be difficult to get down through 5.5 percent, where there are a lot of buyers, before the figures."
May Bund options on the June Bund futures were trading at a volatility of 5.75 percent, while June was at 5.65 percent. Both were down about 0.2 percent from the prior day's trade.
June Bund futures were down nine basis points at 100.19 by 1417 GMT.
A trader at a major British brokerage said interest was clustered in the June series. A European bank traded the 98.00/99.00 put spread 1,500 times, and also bought the 98.50 puts.
"Overall they are pretty negative of the market," said the trader. "We've seen a few bearish trades today."
More than 1,800 lots were traded in the June 98.00 puts, more than 2,900 at the 98.50 and more than 2,600 at the 99.00 strike.
